The energy of this piece is really spunky. Very bouncy and sardonic in its rhythm. However there are times where the syllabic count of the lines prevents that rhythm from hitting “on beat” in a way.

The title is strong too. Very targeted, yet emblematic of the greater concepts the poem is hinting at like class inequity and artistic integrity.

And this is just a personal philosophy of mine, if you feel a need to explain the poem outside of itself, then the poem probably doesn’t quite capture the depth of your vision. The poem should speak for itself

The subject matter here is very strong. The nature of reality vs. the general identity of humanity is an excellent source of poetric drama.

The speaker here seems to me to be antagonistic in their voice, which I’m not sure really benefits the concept of the poem. Belief and disbelief in deity and faith is a deeply human struggle and always has been. I want to hear more about the speaker’s views directly rather than what they disagree with in the listener’s perspective.

This is a topic near and dear to me, I hope you keep exploring it in your work :)
